Policy on greeting routines
After reading you will know how the first steps go
This page matters because the first greeting sets the tone for every pet and traveler who comes to the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways. New staff should open with a calm voice, steady posture, and simple words that help people feel welcome right away. Keep your focus on the animal as well as the traveler, since both may be nervous when they arrive.

Start by noticing the pet before you speak about forms or travel details. A soft greeting, a slow approach, and a little space can make a big difference. If the animal is alert, shy, or uneasy, match your pace to that mood and avoid sudden moves. The goal is to show that we are ready to help without crowding or rushing.

When you check in a pet, use the same respectful manner each time. Make eye contact with the traveler, speak clearly, and keep your hands visible until it is welcome to proceed. If the pet seems worried, do not push ahead with a loud or busy routine. Instead, guide the interaction step by step and let the animal settle. The desk is built for patient attention, and that patience should be easy to feel from the first moment.

<<FACT F034>> You should place the traveler at ease while you confirm the basic travel needs and continue with the usual intake flow. If anything looks unusual, pause and bring in the senior coordinator rather than trying to force a quick answer. Calm review keeps the desk humane and keeps the animal safer.

For onboard care on Halcyon, <<FACT F049>> After that, continue the handoff in the same calm style, using simple directions and a steady pace so the traveler knows what comes next. Never use rough handling, never raise your voice, and never treat the pet like cargo.

Remember that a good greeting is not just polite, it is the first step in safe care.
